strings.name: Ward Cunningham
strings.summary: Ward Cunningham developed the first wiki, advancing collaborative writing, and contributed to software design patterns, extreme programming and agile methods. He explored design and teaching with Kent Beck and later initiated Federated Wiki for sharing across sites. These communities and methods evolved through many contributors.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Wiki and Wikipedia, and collaborative and individual contributions, are distinguished. Historical employers are not presented as current; the disputed birth city is omitted.
strings.influence.rationale: Invented wiki collaboration and contributed to software design methods, influencing open knowledge and software-engineering communities.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Purdue bachelor’s in interdisciplinary engineering and master’s in computer science; separate unconfirmed degree years are omitted.
strings.facts.f2.label: Collaboration model
strings.facts.f2.value: Federated Wiki lets independent sites share, copy and modify pages while preserving provenance and change history.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Opening wiki collaboration
strings.highlights.h1.text: Created the reader-editable WikiWikiWeb for software-pattern discussions, influencing later collaborative websites.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Exploring software design together
strings.highlights.h2.text: Studied pattern languages and CRC cards with Kent Beck to help developers discuss object responsibilities and collaboration.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Recalls pattern repository history for researchers
strings.timeline.t1.text: A public paper by Wirfs-Brock and Hvatum records email correspondence with him about the Portland Pattern Repository on this date; private emails were not directly inspected.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Wiki anniversary interview released
strings.timeline.t2.text: Between the Brackets publishes his reflections on wiki and Federated Wiki; this is the episode release date.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Initiates Federated Wiki
strings.timeline.t3.text: Develops Smallest Federated Wiki with M. Edward Borasky at IndieWebCamp, exploring forking and sharing across sites.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-signs Agile Manifesto
strings.timeline.t4.text: Helps formulate the Manifesto for Agile Software Development as one of seventeen co-authors at Snowbird.
strings.timeline.t5.title: WikiWikiWeb launches publicly
strings.timeline.t5.text: Launches a collaborative site for the patterns community on c2.com; it precedes Wikipedia and is a separate project.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Records software debt metaphor
strings.timeline.t6.text: The WyCash report relates incremental development and later code consolidation through debt; the date is from the manuscript.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-publishes CRC cards paper
strings.timeline.t7.text: With Kent Beck, presents teaching object design through classes, responsibilities and collaboration in an OOPSLA paper.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Co-authors pattern-language report
strings.timeline.t8.text: With Kent Beck, applies Christopher Alexander’s pattern ideas to object-oriented programs; this is the report date, not a conference date.
